posts.title: Five checks before typhoon season
posts.excerpt: Ten minutes with your policy now saves a long month later.
posts.content:
Find your policy and look for one word: water. Many fire policies cover wind but not flooding, and the difference only shows after the river rises.

Then take photos of every room, keep receipts for large items in one folder and save our claims line in your phone. If you are not sure what you have, bring the papers in and we will read them with you.

posts.title: What happens after you call us
posts.excerpt: A claim, from the first phone call to the money in your account.
posts.content:
When you call, the person who answers writes down what happened and opens the claim with your insurer the same day. Your own adviser calls you back the next morning.

We then gather the photos and receipts, meet the insurer’s assessor with you if needed, and check the offer line by line before you accept it. Most home claims close within six weeks.

posts.title: Insuring a small shop, one walk-through at a time
posts.excerpt: The best policy for a shop starts at the front step.
posts.content:
This autumn we walked through a bakery, a bicycle repair shop and a small dental office. Each owner thought they needed more cover; two of them were paying twice for the same thing.

We put each shop on one contract with one renewal date, and wrote a single page they can pin by the till: who to call, what to photograph and what not to throw away after a leak or a break-in.
